title: Microkernel pipelining + KV prefetch for mixed INT8/FP8 late-dequant fusion
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Introduces microkernel pipelining and KV prefetch to improve mixed INT8/FP8 inference throughput and p99 latency. Default behavior is behind runtime feature flag; safe rollback available. Recommended to enable for workloads using long KV caches (chat/decoder-heavy).
description: Motivation: customer workloads (large-decoder chat and retrieval-augmented generation) show inefficiencies when the runtime alternates between quantized microkernels and dequant/requant boundaries. Small kernels suffer from stall time waiting on KV lookups and on-host dequant stages. This PR introduces a microkernel pipelining scheduler plus a KV prefetcher and a late-dequant fusion pass to reduce stalls and amortize dequant overhead across multiple heads. Design highlights: 1) Microkernel pipelining - split GEMM microkernels into producer/consumer stages and schedule them so compute overlaps with memory ops; 2) KV prefetcher - heuristics that prefetch KV ranges for the next N tokens based on sequence-progress predictions and batch alignment; 3) Late-dequant fusion - delay dequant/requant to coalesce adjacent dequant ops and run a single fused conversion where safe; 4) Runtime flags and compatibility - feature gated behind EXP_MICROPIPE and EXP_KV_PREFETCH with graceful fallback to existing pipeline when heuristic not met. Commits summary: "Initial microkernel pipeline scaffolding and scheduler hooks", "Add KV prefetcher + telemetry and unit tests", "Late-dequant fusion pass and correctness guards", "Microbenchmark harness and perf numbers", "Integration tests and canary rollout config". Files changed (high-level): updated runtime kernel registration and microkernel entrypoints, scheduler pipeline module, kv cache prefetcher and heuristics, quantization fusion / graph transform, unit and perf tests, docs with rollout notes. Performance: synthetic and canary benchmarks show median throughput improvement of 12-18% on g4dn-like instances for mixed INT8/FP8 decoder workloads at batch sizes 1-8; p99 token latency reduced by 8-12% in steady-state; GPU memory transient peaks reduced ~6% due to aggregated dequant buffers. Bench harness: 95th-percentile improvements measured on the internal perf-lab with sequence length 1024, 8-headed GPT-like model, measured over 5k steps. Correctness and safety: added deterministic guards around fusion (checks layer types, quant params and overflow safety), unit tests for numeric parity (within tolerance) and a stratified regression set used by Redwood Optimize. Rollout plan: staged canary (5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to eval prompt sets (Linear ENG-7890). Observability: new metrics microkernel.pipeline_util, kv.prefetch.hit_rate and quant.fusion_skipped_reasons. Operational notes: default off for Private installs; enable via runtime config in Dedicated and Hosted per-tenant; telemetry included to evaluate economic impact. Misc: addressed several edge cases called out during review (odd token-length boundaries, multi-GPU sharding misalignment), and added a short-lived compatibility shim that translates old kernel names to the new pipelined entrypoints to avoid breaking pinned model versions.
